thread:
tanvi-support: FYI getting a Priority 1 from AcmeHealth — their Private VPC app started returning 401s and 502s about 08:12 UTC after a maintenance window. They say API calls to our hosted control plane succeed, but calls to their private inference endpoints time out or error.

acmehealth-sre: We saw degraded responses from the deployment to the model endpoint. Error in client logs: "tls: handshake failure" and intermittent 502 from nginx. No recent config changes on our side. Started when DirectConnect maintenance was supposed to complete.

leo-netops: @tanvi-support can you confirm whether traffic is going over ExpressRoute/DirectConnect or IPsec? Also need to know if private control plane or VPC peering was in use.

tanvi-support: Customer is on Redwood Private (VPC) with Direct Connect (DX) into our transit. They have a site-to-site IPsec fallback too but DX is primary. Control plane reachable; only inference nodes in their VPC failing.

rhonda-eng-oncall: Thanks. Can you share a traceroute + curl from a test host in the customer's VPC to one of the failing inference nodes? Prefer a curl with -v so we see the TLS error.

acmehealth-sre: Pasting sanitized output: 

```
$ curl -v https://10.20.45.12/api/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer xxx"\n* Connected to 10.20.45.12 (10.20.45.12) port 443 (#0)\n* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256\n* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure\n* Closing connection 0\n```

and traceroute: 

```
traceroute to 10.20.45.12 (10.20.45.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.7 ms  0.6 ms  0.6 ms
 2  dx-gw-1.example  2.1 ms  2.3 ms  2.2 ms
 3  redwood-transit-gw  3.5 ms  3.8 ms  3.6 ms
 4  10.20.45.12  4.0 ms  4.1 ms  4.0 ms
```

leo-netops: Traceroute looks fine. The TLS handshake failure suggests mismatched cipher suites or client cert issue. Did we rotate any intermediate CA or alter allowed ciphers on the inference side?

ivan-plat: We didn't rotate certs recently for that model fleet. However we did push an nginx upgrade last week that tightened TLS defaults (disabled TLS1.0/1.1, removed some legacy ciphers). Could be the upstream VPN/TS-terminator device not negotiating a compatible suite.

acmehealth-sre: Note their on-prem firewall/edge doesn't do TLS termination, it's passthrough. Customer confirmed they recently patched their edge appliances with a vendor update that changed IPsec crypto policy.

rhonda-eng-oncall: Two likely vectors: 1) DX route path changed to fall back to IPsec device that does TLS interception or uses an older cipher; 2) MTU or fragmentation causing TLS handshake fragments to drop (sometimes results in handshake failure). Let's check MSS/DF and whether UDP fragmentation (for IPsec NAT-T) is happening.

tanvi-support: I asked customer to run a quick tcpdump on their edge while we reproduce a failing curl. They returned this snippet showing ESP with NAT-T and occasional ICMP frag-needed messages: 

```
12:11:57.123 IP our-client > 10.20.45.12: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 229, length 511
12:11:57.124 IP 192.0.2.5 > 198.51.100.1: ESP(spi=0x1a2b3c)
12:11:57.125 IP 192.0.2.5 > 198.51.100.1: UDP(4500)
12:11:57.126 ICMP 10.20.45.12 udp port 4500 unreachable, message: fragmentation needed and DF set
```

leo-netops: That ICMP frag-needed is the smoking gun for MTU/MSS. If DF is set and ICMP is blocked anywhere along path (e.g., our egress allowlist or customer firewall), PMTUD will fail and TLS handshake can break due to large ClientHello + certs.

ivan-plat: On Redwood Private, we have an egress allowlist for management endpoints; I need to confirm whether we block ICMP type 3 code 4 on our transit. Our usual policy allows ICMP, but some ACLs for DX peers might be restrictive. I'll query infra rules now.

sre-bot: Incident created: RI-2026-0423-1125, severity=P1, affected=AcmeHealth Private deployment, tags=[dx,ipsec,mtu,tls].

rhonda-eng-oncall: Meanwhile, @acmehealth-sre please try forcing a lower MTU on the client to 1400 and retry curl (or set TCP MSS clamping on their edge). That often mitigates the handshake problem quickly.

acmehealth-sre: Tried MTU 1400 — TLS handshake completes and API returns 200. So MTU fragmentation confirmed as root cause.

tanvi-support: Great. Next steps: 1) We should add a KB for customers using DX+IPsec fallback recommending MSS clamping or allow ICMP frag-needed on transit. 2) Ivan, please confirm and, if necessary, update our DX ACLs to permit ICMP type 3/code 4 or add an explicit path MTU clamp on the transit gateway. 3) Customer will roll a temporary MSS clamp on their edge until we remediate.

ivan-plat: I'll escalate to infra team and paste the ACL diff here. If we can't change ACLs quickly, we can add a route-mangle step on the transit to clamp MSS to 1420 as a short-term fix.

rhonda-eng-oncall: Also add a note about TLS handshake sizes in the KB — some model endpoints send larger cert chains (client + intermediate) during mutual TLS flows which increases susceptibility to MTU problems.

tanvi-support: Noted. I'll keep this thread updated. AcmeHealth confirmed they can work with the temporary clamp and will watch for regressions. Thanks all :thumbsup:

acmehealth-sre: Thanks for the quick help. Will file follow-up with our edge vendor on the IPsec crypto policy that changed.

ivan-plat: ACLs updated: allowed ICMP type 3 code 4 on DX peer to/from 192.0.2.0/24. Deploying transit MSS clamp as fallback.

rhonda-eng-oncall: Marking incident as mitigated pending infra deploy. Leave open for postmortem and KB items.

sre-bot: Incident RI-2026-0423-1125 status=mitigated, mitigation_time=1745557350
